Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: 3-day hx diarrhea; “very watery” initially, now very loose; causing abdominal pain

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Diarrhea initially very watery, now very loose
Diarrhea frequency has been so frequent the patient lost count, at least four times today
Subjective fever described as feeling 'boiling' without thermometer measurement
Vomiting of everything including water and tea
Last episode of vomiting was approximately 2 hours ago after attempting breakfast
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: last emesis ~2h ago after attempting breakfast

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Periumbilical abdominal pain that is very sore and intermittent
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Pain: periumbilical (around navel), very sore; intermittent

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Periumbilical pain associated with urges to open bowels during episodes
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: urges to open bowels with episodes

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient is passing urine normally with last urination about 1 hour ago
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Urine: passing urine OK; last passed ~1h ago

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Urine colour has not been observed
Baseline bowel habit is once daily and normal
No usual history of diarrhea or constipation at baseline
Brother has similar symptoms and patient reports many at school are affected
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Sick contacts: brother with similar sx; reports “everyone in school’s got this”

Medications.content: Takes ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps
Using oral rehydration solution approximately three times per day for two days
Medications.source_text: ORS (salt-sugar) ~3x/day x2 days (not helping due to vomiting)

Social_and_Family_History.content: Occasional alcohol use, described as an occasional pint
Last menstrual period approximately two weeks ago
Working from home today due to illness

Assessment.source_text: 1) Acute gastroenteritis—3d watery→loose diarrhea, N/V (cannot keep fluids), subjective fever, periumbilical pain; sick contact; no blood in stool/urine; urinating OK

Assessment.content: Dehydration risk secondary to vomiting and diarrhea

Plan_of_Care.content: Continue oral rehydration solution in very small, frequent sips
Plan_of_Care.source_text: ORS: continue very small, frequent sips

Plan_of_Care.content: Simple diet with toast or biscuits
Arrange urgent clinic appointment via support line for hydration assessment
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Urgent clinic appt via support line for hydration assessment

Plan_of_Care.content: Obtain stool sample to rule out bacterial infection and treat if indicated
Plan_of_Care.source_text: and stool sample (r/o bacterial infection; treat if indicated)

Plan_of_Care.content: If symptoms worsen or patient feels more unwell, attend A&E
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Safety-net: if worsening/feel more unwell, attend A&E

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient may call back in the meantime
Plan_of_Care.source_text: may call back in the meantime

Follow_up_Information.content: Urgent clinic appointment to be arranged via support line
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Urgent clinic appt via support line for hydration assessment and stool sample

Review_of_Systems.source_text: Pain: periumbilical (around navel), very sore; intermittent
